title: World-Model Companies Keep Projects Secret
content:
The world‑modeling sector has become a hotbed of venture capital and media attention, with a handful of startups raising hundreds of millions of dollars to build AI systems that map the entire planet. Yet insiders report a pervasive lack of transparency: founders, investors, and even data suppliers are reluctant to disclose the specifics of the models they are training, the data pipelines they rely on, or the intended applications of the technology. This opacity has prompted skepticism among analysts and regulators who question how these systems will be validated and deployed.

Companies that have disclosed funding figures reveal a pattern of rapid scaling. For instance, a leading firm raised $250 million in a Series C round last year, while a competitor secured $180 million in a Series B. Both firms cite “world‑scale data ingestion” as a core capability, but neither has released a product demo or a white paper detailing the architecture. Data suppliers, ranging from satellite imagery providers to crowdsourced mapping services, also remain tight‑lipped, citing proprietary agreements and the potential for competitive advantage. The lack of public benchmarks and performance metrics makes it difficult for third‑party researchers to assess the models’ accuracy, bias, or compliance with privacy regulations.

The industry’s secrecy could slow broader adoption and raise regulatory concerns. Without clear documentation, governments and civil society groups worry about the potential for misuse, from surveillance to environmental monitoring. As the sector continues to attract capital, stakeholders are calling for greater disclosure and independent audits to ensure that the promised benefits of comprehensive world models are realized responsibly.
author: TechCrunch

title: Angle Health reaches $2.7B valuation after growing to 5,000 customers
content:
Angle Health, a health‑insurance technology company, has reached a milestone of 5,000 small‑business customers and announced that it has become profitable. The firm’s growth has been driven by its level‑funded insurance model, which blends features of traditional self‑funded plans with the simplicity of fully insured coverage. By allowing employers to set a predictable monthly premium while still benefiting from potential cost savings, the model has appealed to small businesses seeking both control and affordability.

The company’s expansion reflects a broader shift in the small‑business health‑insurance market, where many employers are looking for alternatives to the high costs and administrative burdens of fully insured plans. Angle Health’s platform offers automated claims processing, real‑time cost tracking, and a single‑page dashboard that simplifies the experience for both employers and employees. With profitability now achieved, the firm plans to scale its technology and customer support to serve an even larger segment of the small‑business community.
author: TechCrunch

title: Automattic Appoints Jeremy Klaperman as Interim CFO
content:
WordPress VIP Enterprise has announced that Jeremy Klaperman, the company’s current Chief Financial Officer, will serve as acting CFO on an interim basis. Klaperman, who has overseen the financial strategy of the enterprise division, will maintain the unit’s fiscal oversight while the organization searches for a permanent replacement.

The decision follows the recent departure of the former CFO, and the company confirmed that Klaperman’s appointment is intended to ensure continuity of financial operations and stakeholder confidence during the transition. He will continue to manage budgeting, reporting, and compliance functions, and will report to the senior leadership team on key financial metrics.

WordPress VIP Enterprise expects the search for a full‑time CFO to be completed within the next few months. In the meantime, Klaperman’s experience within the company positions him to guide the enterprise division through this period of change while maintaining its financial stability.
author: TechCrunch

title: Accenture to Lead Anthropic's First Embedded Evaluator Project
content:
Accenture has announced that it is preparing to launch its most high‑risk consulting engagement to date, a multi‑year technology transformation for a leading national government agency. The project, valued at more than $1.2 billion, will overhaul the agency’s legacy systems, integrate advanced data analytics, and implement a cloud‑native infrastructure to support critical public services. The engagement is considered high risk because it involves a tight 18‑month delivery window, strict regulatory compliance requirements, and the need to maintain uninterrupted service for millions of citizens.

Key details of the initiative include a phased migration strategy that will run parallel to the existing operations, a partnership with a major cloud provider, and the deployment of artificial‑intelligence tools for real‑time risk monitoring. Accenture will leverage its global delivery network and industry‑specific expertise to manage the complex change‑management and cybersecurity challenges inherent in such a large‑scale overhaul. The client’s executive team has emphasized that any delay or failure could result in significant financial penalties and reputational damage, underscoring the high stakes of the engagement.

In conclusion, Accenture’s willingness to undertake this ambitious project signals its confidence in its capabilities and its commitment to delivering transformative solutions under demanding conditions. If successful, the engagement could set a new benchmark for public‑sector digital transformation and reinforce Accenture’s position as a trusted partner for high‑stakes initiatives worldwide.
author: TechCrunch

title: Trump threatens to bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House
content:
The president has escalated a series of lawsuits targeting major international news outlets, adding The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the BBC to a growing list of media organizations facing legal action. The filings, submitted this week in federal court, allege that the outlets published false statements that harmed the administration’s reputation and interfered with its policy agenda.

The new suits follow earlier proceedings in which the president’s legal team sought injunctions and damages from other publishers for similar claims of defamation and misinformation. Court documents indicate that the complaints focus on specific articles and broadcasts released over the past twelve months, asserting that the content violated U.S. libel standards. Legal analysts note that the cases could set precedents for how public officials challenge media reporting, while the defendants maintain that their reporting is protected under the First Amendment. The outcomes of these actions are expected to shape the ongoing tension between the executive branch and the press.
author: Euronews

title: Saudi seeks allies amid Houthi attacks, Russia holds parliamentary vote, AI chief warns of risks, UK royalty responds to Diana claims
content:
This week’s headlines spanned the Middle East, Europe, technology and the United Kingdom, underscoring a blend of security, political and corporate concerns. Saudi Arabia appealed to regional allies for military assistance as Iran‑backed Houthi forces tightened control over Yemen’s Red Sea coastline and the Bab el‑Mandeb strait, while a series of drone strikes on Saudi oil facilities intensified an emerging energy‑supply strain. In Russia, voters participated in a tightly managed parliamentary election that featured minimal opposition, and President Vladimir Putin reiterated that the country would not initiate a new mobilisation of troops.

Concurrently, internal warnings about artificial‑intelligence risks surfaced from within the industry. Microsoft’s AI chief Mustafa Suleyman cautioned against anthropomorphising AI models and suggested that a future “silicon species” could compete with humans for resources, highlighting growing regulatory and ethical debates. In the United Kingdom, the royal family faced renewed scrutiny after Earl Spencer issued fresh claims regarding Princess Diana’s funeral, prompting a sharply worded rebuttal from Buckingham Palace that emphasized factual accuracy and the family’s desire for privacy.

These developments illustrate the interconnected challenges confronting governments, corporations and public institutions. The heightened military tension in the Red Sea, the controlled political environment in Russia, the emerging discourse on AI governance, and the sensitivity surrounding the British monarchy each demand close observation as they shape regional stability, technological policy and public confidence.
author: France 24

title: Trump bans CNN, MSNOW, Politico from White House
content:
Washington – On Friday, President Donald Trump announced that CNN, MSNOW and Politico would be barred from White House press briefings, citing what he described as consistently unfavorable coverage. The decision, presented as a test of the First Amendment’s protection of press freedom, marks the latest instance in which the administration has taken punitive action against news organizations it deems hostile.

Legal scholars and press freedom advocates warned that the move could set a precedent for restricting access based on editorial stance rather than legitimate security concerns. The White House has not detailed specific criteria for the ban, and the affected outlets have pledged to continue covering the administration through alternative channels. The development adds to ongoing debates over the balance between presidential authority and constitutional guarantees for a free press.
author: France 24

title: UEFA and CONCACAF request FIFA release $2.1 billion for member associations
content:
UEFA and CONCACAF leaders have jointly appealed to FIFA President Gianni Infantino to allocate roughly $2.1 billion from the organization’s reserve funds, proposing that each of the 211 member associations receive $10 million for the 2027‑2030 competition cycle. The request was presented at a recent meeting of the two confederations and underscores a push for broader financial support across global football bodies ahead of the next World Cup cycle.  

The demand emerges amid ongoing tensions surrounding Infantino’s earlier plan to sell a minority stake in the World Cup to private investors—a proposal that was abandoned after strong opposition from European clubs and leagues. By redirecting existing reserves rather than pursuing new commercial partnerships, the confederations aim to address funding disparities while avoiding further controversy over the sport’s governance and commercial direction.
author: France 24

title: 37 detainees die in custody during illegal mining probe in Niger State, Nigeria
content:
Tonight’s broadcast focused on three distinct developments across Africa and the literary world. In Nigeria, authorities have launched an ongoing investigation into the deaths of thirty‑seven individuals who were detained on accusations of illegal mining, a case that has drawn scrutiny from human‑rights groups and prompted calls for a transparent inquiry. Meanwhile, Tunisia is gaining recognition as a burgeoning boat‑building hub, with local shipyards expanding capacity to meet demand from domestic customers and international markets, signaling a potential shift in regional maritime manufacturing. The program also featured an interview with Ricci Shryock, author of the newly released novel “The Moon Will Not Burn Us,” in which she discussed the book’s themes and her creative process.

These stories underscore a range of socio‑economic dynamics: the Nigerian investigation highlights ongoing concerns about custodial safety and the enforcement of mining regulations; Tunisia’s maritime industry growth points to diversification of its economy and increased export potential; and Shryock’s literary contribution adds to contemporary discourse on resilience and hope. The broadcast concluded by emphasizing the importance of continued monitoring of these developments and the broader implications they hold for the respective regions.
author: France 24

title: Houthis rise as Iran's leading regional proxy after Yemen victories
content:
The Houthi movement in Yemen has emerged as a more prominent actor in the ongoing U.S.–Iran confrontation, overtaking Lebanon’s Hezbollah as the leading component of Iran’s so‑called “axis of resistance.” Recent battlefield successes against Yemeni government forces and coalition partners have expanded the group’s operational reach, prompting U.S. officials to reassess the strategic weight of the Houthis within Tehran’s regional proxy network.

Analysts note that the shift reflects Tehran’s broader effort to diversify its influence across the Red Sea and the Arabian Peninsula, where the Houthis have demonstrated the capacity to threaten shipping lanes and conduct missile strikes. While Hezbollah remains a key ally in the Levant, the heightened visibility of the Houthis underscores a recalibration of Iran’s proxy strategy, suggesting that future U.S. policy and military planning will increasingly account for the Yemeni group’s growing role in the regional power balance.
author: DW World

title: Lebanese artist repurposes missile debris into artwork
content:
Visual artist Lina Jouni, who lives and works in southern Lebanon, has begun converting material salvaged from Israeli missile strikes into sculptural and mixed‑media pieces. The debris, which includes fragments of concrete, metal shrapnel and other remnants recovered from damaged homes and infrastructure, is collected by Jouni and local volunteers in the aftermath of each attack. She then incorporates the fragments into artworks that are displayed in community centers and galleries across the region, aiming to document the physical traces of the ongoing hostilities.

Jouni’s practice has attracted attention from humanitarian organizations and cultural institutions that are documenting the conflict’s impact on civilian life. Exhibitions of her work have been scheduled in Beirut and in a temporary space in the town of Tyre, where the pieces are accompanied by informational panels describing the origin of the materials. By repurposing the remnants of destruction, the artist provides a tangible record of the missile strikes while offering a visual narrative that underscores the resilience of affected communities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russia designates Cannes director Andrey Zvyagintsev as foreign agent
content:
Acclaimed Russian filmmaker Ivan Petrov, whose film *The Silent River* captured the 2026 Grand Prix award at the Cannes Film Festival, has drawn renewed international attention for his outspoken criticism of Russia’s military invasion of Ukraine. The Cannes jury highlighted Petrov’s work for its artistic innovation and poignant storytelling, noting that the director’s reputation for tackling socially charged subjects has long set him apart in contemporary cinema. In a recent interview with a European news outlet, Petrov condemned the conflict, describing it as “a tragic breach of human rights and a profound threat to cultural dialogue,” and called for an immediate cease‑fire and diplomatic resolution.

Petrov’s statements have sparked a mixed response within Russia’s cultural sphere, where officials have previously warned artists against public dissent. While some Russian film industry peers have expressed support for his anti‑war stance, state‑affiliated media have labeled his remarks “unpatriotic.” International observers, including representatives from the European Union and UNESCO, have praised Petrov’s courage in using his platform to advocate for peace, emphasizing the broader role of artists in shaping public discourse. The director’s dual recognition—both as a Cannes laureate and as a vocal critic of the war—underscores the complex interplay between cultural achievement and political expression in today’s global landscape.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump bans CNN, MSNBC and Politico from White House
content:
Washington — The White House announced new restrictions on media access after President Joe Biden said that certain outlets have been “publishing fiction and lies.” In a briefing on Thursday, the president declared that any organization deemed to repeatedly disseminate false information will lose its White House press credentials and be barred from attending briefings, receiving official statements, or requesting interviews with senior staff. The policy, which will be administered by an internal review panel, requires the affected outlets to submit a formal appeal within 10 days; pending the outcome, their reporters will be excluded from the press pool and denied entry to the West Wing.

Press organizations and civil‑liberties groups have criticized the move as a threat to the free flow of information, warning that the criteria for “fiction” are vague and could be used to silence dissent. The White House Press Secretary defended the action, saying it is intended to protect the public from misinformation and to ensure that journalists adhere to established fact‑checking standards. As the new rules take effect, the debate over balancing accurate reporting with press freedom is expected to intensify.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Syria arrests five former al‑Assad‑era air officers
content:
Former senior officers of the national air force, among them a retired general, were taken into custody during a coordinated series of police operations announced on Tuesday. The arrests were carried out by the country's anti‑corruption bureau in conjunction with the military police, and were described in an official press release as part of an ongoing investigation into alleged misconduct by former members of the armed forces.

Authorities said the detained individuals are being questioned on charges that include abuse of authority and illicit procurement activities while they held command positions. The operations, which spanned several locations, underscore a broader governmental effort to address corruption within the defense establishment. The investigation remains active, and the officials involved have not yet entered pleas, with further developments expected in the coming weeks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Assala Nasri returns to Damascus for sold‑out concert after 15‑year exile
content:
Thousands of people gathered at the Al‑Mansour Cultural Center in Damascus on Saturday, creating a thunderous welcome for Syrian singer Assala Nasri as she took the stage for a sold‑out concert. The event, organized by the Ministry of Culture in partnership with local promoters, marked the artist’s first public performance in the capital after a five‑year hiatus abroad, drawing an audience that filled the venue’s 5,000‑seat capacity.

Assala, renowned for her contributions to Arabic pop and classical music since the early 1990s, performed a repertoire that spanned her early hits and recent releases, accompanied by a live orchestra and a supporting band. Security measures were heightened, and the concert proceeded without incident, reflecting both the logistical coordination of the organizers and the public’s enthusiasm for the return of a cultural figure whose career has been intertwined with Syria’s modern musical landscape. The successful turnout underscores a renewed appetite for live entertainment in the country and highlights the role of prominent artists in fostering cultural engagement.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK court acquits woman of supporting Hamas in university speech
content:
Sarah Cotte, a public commentator, clarified that her recent remarks were intended to endorse the Palestinian right to resist occupation rather than to express support for Hamas. In a statement released after the comments sparked debate on social media, Cotte emphasized that her language was aimed at highlighting broader issues of self‑determination and resistance, distinguishing her stance from any endorsement of the militant group’s tactics or ideology.

The clarification follows a wave of criticism from observers who interpreted her words as aligning with Hamas, prompting discussions about the boundaries of political expression and the sensitivities surrounding the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict. Cotte’s response underscores the ongoing challenge for public figures to navigate nuanced positions on contentious topics while addressing concerns about potential misinterpretation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Germany receives first F-35 fighter jet from the United States
content:
Germany’s air force took delivery of the first of an anticipated fleet of nearly three dozen F‑35 stealth fighters from Lockheed Martin on Tuesday, marking the initial fulfillment of a procurement program launched four years ago. The aircraft, part of a multi‑year contract signed in 2022 for approximately 35 jets, are slated to replace aging Eurofighter Typhoons and bolster Germany’s contribution to NATO’s collective air‑defence capabilities. The delivery ceremony, held at the Lockheed Martin facility in Fort Worth, Texas, was attended by senior German defense officials and representatives of the U.S. Department of Defense, underscoring the strategic partnership underpinning the acquisition.

The remaining aircraft are scheduled for phased delivery through 2030, with the German Ministry of Defence planning to integrate the fifth‑generation platform into its operational units after a series of flight‑testing and crew‑training programs. The procurement, valued at roughly €10 billion, is intended to enhance Germany’s ability to conduct air‑dominance, strike, and intelligence‑surveillance‑reconnaissance missions, aligning the nation’s air capabilities with those of its NATO allies. The arrival of the first F‑35 signals the start of a modernization effort that will reshape Germany’s aerial combat posture over the coming decade.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Organisers apologize after North Korean anthem played for South Korean team at Asian Games
content:
Organisers of the Asian Games in Japan have issued an apology after the North Korean national anthem was mistakenly played for the South Korean men’s hockey team during a competition ceremony. The error occurred during the opening of the South Korea‑Japan match, where the anthem intended to honor the South Korean squad was incorrectly selected from the event’s music library, prompting immediate confusion among athletes and spectators.

The Games’ organizing committee said the mistake was “unacceptable” and attributed it to a technical oversight, promising a review of protocols to prevent similar incidents. South Korean officials expressed disappointment but accepted the apology, emphasizing the importance of respecting national symbols in international sport. The committee reaffirmed its commitment to accurate representation of all participating nations as the Games continue.
author: BBC World

title: Kennedy Center reports surplus after 2024 financial review
content:
Records released for 2024 indicate that the venue posted a surplus of several million dollars after accounting for contributions and grant funding. The financial statements show that, once these external sources of revenue were incorporated, the net result was a positive balance that exceeds the operating costs for the year.

The surplus underscores the venue’s fiscal stability and may influence budgeting decisions and program planning for upcoming periods. Officials noted that the additional funds provide flexibility for future investments, maintenance, and potential community initiatives.
author: BBC World

title: Trump announces ban on CNN and Politico from White House
content:
Washington — The president’s relationship with the national press has been marked by persistent tension and confrontational rhetoric since he entered public office. Beginning with his 2015 campaign launch, he routinely accused mainstream outlets of bias, labeling unfavorable coverage as “fake news” and “the enemy of the people.” Throughout his tenure as a congressman and later as a governor, he held press conferences that frequently devolved into sharp exchanges, and his social‑media posts often singled out individual journalists for criticism. The pattern continued after his election to the White House, where he regularly dismissed daily briefings, reduced the frequency of formal press interactions, and pursued legal actions against media organizations alleging defamation.

During his administration, the president’s approach to the media influenced both policy and public discourse. He instituted a “media blacklist” that limited access for outlets deemed hostile, and his communications office issued daily statements that framed coverage disputes as part of a broader struggle over truth. Congressional hearings examined the impact of these tactics on press freedom, while watchdog groups reported an increase in threats against reporters covering the White House. As the president approaches the end of his term, the longstanding adversarial dynamic remains a defining feature of his political legacy, underscoring ongoing debates about the role of a free press in a democratic society.
author: BBC World

title: Karol G review – Colombian chart-topper brings pan-Latin camp and fireworks to New Jersey
content:
MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, hosted the first night of Karol G’s Viajando por el Mundo Tropitour on Thursday, marking the Colombian superstar’s return to the venue after headline­ing it in September 2023 as the first Latina to do so. The concert was billed as a spectacle of glamor and energy, with the artist’s stage production featuring dazzling lights, high‑energy choreography and a setlist that spanned her chart‑topping hits.

The venue, known for its large‑scale sporting events, proved a fitting backdrop for the tour’s theatrical flair. Karol G’s performance was described as a “convincing argument for suspending disbelief,” as she blended Latin pop with urban influences while engaging a crowd that filled the stadium to capacity. The show’s production elements—costume changes, pyrotechnics, and a visually striking backdrop—underscored the artist’s reputation for high‑concept live shows.

With a second night scheduled, the tour is poised to continue drawing fans across the region. Karol G’s presence at MetLife Stadium not only highlights her status as a leading figure in Latin music but also demonstrates the venue’s versatility beyond sports, cementing her role as a major draw for large‑audience performances.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Trent Alexander-Arnold recalled by England but with a warning from Thomas Tuchel
content:
Trent Alexander‑Arnold has been recalled to the England squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches, prompting head coach Thomas Tuchel to emphasize the need for defensive solidity. The right‑back, who has only represented England once before – in June last year against Andorra and Senegal – will now be expected to bring a more disciplined defensive approach to the team.

Tuchel’s decision comes after a period of scrutiny over Alexander‑Arnold’s defensive lapses, which could jeopardise England’s World Cup campaign if not addressed. By urging the player to focus on his back‑line contributions, the coach signals a shift toward a more balanced side, hoping to reduce the risk of defensive errors in high‑stakes fixtures.

With the Nations League fixtures on the horizon, England will rely on Alexander‑Arnold’s improved defensive work to support the squad’s overall solidity, a key factor in the team’s pursuit of success on the international stage.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England beat Sri Lanka by six wickets in Cardiff to win T20 series
content:
England comfortably beat Sri Lanka by six wickets in Cardiff, clinching the T20 series with a match to spare. The match, played at the County Ground, saw England chase a modest target after a solid opening partnership that set the tone for the innings. Sri Lanka were bowled out for a sub‑par total, with England’s bowlers exploiting the conditions to restrict the hosts to a low score.

England’s victory was built on a disciplined bowling display, with the frontline bowlers taking key wickets early and maintaining pressure throughout the innings. The batting side capitalised on the wickets, with a steady partnership that ensured a comfortable chase. Sri Lanka struggled to adapt to the pitch and the English bowling attack, and their batting lineup failed to produce the runs required to keep the match competitive.

The win extends England’s strong T20 form and boosts their standing in the ICC rankings. With the series secured, both teams will look ahead to upcoming fixtures, while England’s confidence is set to carry into future international contests.
author: BBC Sport

title: Allen Leads Bills to 41-31 Victory Over Lions in New Stadium
content:
Buffalo secured a decisive 41‑31 victory over the Detroit Lions in the inaugural game at the new Highmark Stadium. Quarterback Josh Allen was the star of the day, throwing six touchdown passes and adding a rushing score, while the Bills’ offense moved the ball efficiently and capitalized on key defensive stops.

Allen’s performance was a highlight for the Bills, who combined a balanced attack with a disciplined defense that forced several turnovers and limited Detroit’s scoring opportunities. The Lions struggled to contain Buffalo’s offense, and despite a late rally, they could not overcome the Bills’ early lead and the sustained pressure applied throughout the game.

The win not only gave Buffalo a strong start in their brand‑new home but also underscored the team’s offensive potency and defensive resilience. As the Bills continue to build momentum in the 2026 season, the victory at Highmark Stadium sets a positive tone for the franchise’s future in the new arena.
author: BBC Sport

title: Isak Credits Relationships with Iraola and Gakpo for Season Success
content:
Alexander Isak said that the support he has received from former Real Sociedad coach Andoni Iraola and current Real Madrid teammate Cody Gakpo has been pivotal to his progress this season. In a post‑match interview, the Swedish striker praised Iraola for the tactical foundation he laid during his time at San Sebastián, noting that the lessons on positioning and work ethic have translated into more effective play in the Premier League of Spain.  

Isak also highlighted the camaraderie he has built with Gakpo, whose experience in the Dutch and English leagues has helped him adjust to the pace and physicality of La Liga. He explained that Gakpo’s willingness to share insights on set‑pieces and defensive responsibilities has broadened his understanding of the game, allowing him to contribute more consistently in attack. The combination of Iraola’s strategic guidance and Gakpo’s on‑field mentorship, according to Isak, has been a key factor in his increased confidence and goal‑scoring output.  

Looking ahead, Isak remains focused on maintaining his development trajectory and contributing to Real Madrid’s title ambitions. He expressed gratitude for the relationships that have shaped his season and emphasized the importance of continuing to learn from both former coaches and current teammates as the campaign progresses.
author: BBC Sport

title: Michele Kang Urges Infrastructure Boost for Women’s Sports
content:
London City Lionesses owner Michele Kang has underscored the need for expanded infrastructure in women’s football, citing the club’s recent growth and the broader development of the sport in England. Kang, who joined the Lionesses in 2022, highlighted that adequate training facilities, medical support and stadium upgrades are essential for sustaining competitive performance and attracting top talent to the league.

The Lionesses’ own experience illustrates the gap: the club has struggled to secure a dedicated home ground that meets the standards of the Women’s Super League, forcing players to train in sub‑optimal conditions. Kang argues that investment in purpose‑built facilities would not only improve player welfare and match quality but also boost fan engagement and revenue streams. She urges governing bodies and private investors to prioritise infrastructure as a key lever for elevating women’s football to the same professional level enjoyed by men’s teams.
author: BBC Sport

title: Tuchel Names Alexander-Arnold and Palmer in England Squad
content:
Thomas Tuchel has named his first England squad since the 2026 World Cup, surprising many with the inclusion of two players who had previously been overlooked. The 38‑year‑old manager recalled Liverpool centre‑back Trent Alexander‑Arnold and Crystal Palace midfielder Cole Palmer, both of whom were absent from the squad that finished third in Qatar. Tuchel’s decision signals a shift in his approach to squad selection, prioritising experience and versatility over youth alone.

Alexander‑Arnold, who has been a mainstay in Liverpool’s back line for the past six seasons, brings a wealth of Premier League and European experience to the national side. Palmer, meanwhile, has emerged as a key playmaker for Palace, earning praise for his passing range and work rate. Tuchel’s inclusion of these players comes ahead of England’s upcoming international fixtures, where the team will look to build cohesion after a period of transition following the 2026 World Cup campaign.

The move underscores Tuchel’s intent to blend seasoned talent with emerging prospects as England prepares for the next cycle of international competition. By reintroducing Alexander‑Arnold and Palmer, he aims to strengthen the squad’s defensive solidity and midfield creativity, positioning England for a strong showing in forthcoming tournaments.
author: BBC Sport

title: York Valkyrie Beat Leeds Rhinos to Reach Grand Final
content:
York Valkyrie secured their berth in the Grand Final after a decisive 32‑18 victory over Leeds Rhinos in the semi‑final held at AMT Headingley on Sunday, 20 September 2026. The match, which drew a crowd of over 12,000, saw York’s forwards dominate the middle of the park while the backs exploited gaps in the Rhinos’ defense to create a steady stream of points. Key performances came from captain James O’Connor, who added 18 points through a combination of tries and conversions, and winger Ethan Hughes, who finished with a try and a crucial tackle in the closing minutes.

The win marks a historic moment for York, who have been steadily climbing the Championship ladder since their promotion last season. Facing a Super League‑level opponent, the Valkyrie’s tactical discipline and physicality were on full display, earning praise from analysts who noted the team’s balanced attack and resilient defense. The victory also eliminates a formidable rival, setting up a Grand Final clash against the other semi‑final winner, the Sheffield Eagles, who will look to capitalize on their momentum heading into the final.

With the Grand Final now on the horizon, York’s coaching staff will focus on fine‑tuning their game plan to counter the Eagles’ high‑tempo style. The club’s leadership expressed confidence that the squad’s experience from recent playoff campaigns will serve them well in the decisive match, which is scheduled for Saturday, 4 October 2026 at the national stadium.
author: BBC Sport

title: McIlroy Stays Four Strokes Behind Leader at BMW PGA
content:
Rory McIlroy remains in the hunt at the BMW PGA Championship, recording a five‑under 67 in the second round to finish four strokes behind current leader Ryan Gerard. The Irishman’s score keeps him firmly in contention as the tournament progresses at Wentworth Club.

With Gerard holding the top spot after his own strong round, McIlroy’s performance keeps him within striking distance of the leaderboard. As the championship moves into its final rounds, the gap between the two players will be a key storyline to watch.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump to Announce Nationwide Medicaid Drug Pricing Plan
content:
President Donald Trump is slated to address the nation on Friday with a new initiative aimed at reducing prescription‑drug costs. In the remarks, the president will announce that Medicaid programs in all 50 states will be granted “most‑favored‑nation” pricing for a selected group of medications, a policy designed to align state drug purchases with the lowest prices available internationally. The announcement will be made in the Oval Office, where several governors are expected to join the president to underscore the bipartisan support for the measure.

The proposed pricing framework seeks to leverage the purchasing power of Medicaid to secure lower rates from pharmaceutical manufacturers, potentially saving billions of dollars for state budgets and beneficiaries. Officials indicated that the policy will apply to high‑cost, brand‑name drugs that currently lack competitive pricing, and that the administration will work with Congress and the Department of Health and Human Services to implement the changes. If enacted, the move would mark a significant expansion of the federal government’s efforts to curb drug expenses for low‑income patients across the country.
author: The Hill

title: Claude Drives Over 25% of Anthropic's R&D Efforts
content:
Anthropic announced on Thursday that its flagship chatbot, Claude, now accounts for more than a quarter of the company’s research and development work. The disclosure underscores the growing influence of AI systems within the very teams that create them, a trend that has been hinted at by researchers who argue that the technology is edging closer to autonomous design and improvement.

The company’s internal data shows that Claude’s code‑generation and debugging capabilities are being leveraged to prototype new models, test architectural changes, and refine training pipelines. This shift reflects a broader industry movement toward “AI‑in‑AI” workflows, where machine learning models help accelerate their own development cycles. Analysts note that such practices could shorten iteration times and reduce human oversight, raising both efficiency gains and questions about accountability.

If Anthropic’s approach proves scalable, it could signal a new era in AI development, where chatbots and other generative models play a central role in building the next generation of intelligence. The company’s move highlights the increasing blurring of lines between tool and creator, a dynamic that will likely shape the trajectory of AI research in the coming years.
author: The Hill

title: Vance Criticizes Rob Sand at Iowa Rally
content:
Vice President Mike Vance addressed a crowd in Council Bluffs on Friday, launching a seven‑minute critique of Iowa Democratic gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand. Vance argued that Sand’s progressive positions would make him too far left to govern the state, a claim that followed the vice president’s broader effort to rally Republican voters ahead of the November election. The remarks came as Sand, who has won several statewide polls, is set to face incumbent Republican Governor Kim Reynolds in the race to succeed her.

Sand’s lead in the polls reflects a broader trend of Democratic gains in Iowa’s statewide contests, while Vance’s comments underscore the Republican Party’s strategy to highlight ideological differences between the parties. The Iowa gubernatorial race is now a key battleground for both parties, with the outcome likely to shape the state’s policy direction for the next four years. The vice president’s attack on Sand adds another layer of rhetoric to an already heated campaign.
author: The Hill

title: Fed Review Finds Staff Acknowledged Risks in Silicon Valley Bank Collapse
content:
The Federal Reserve’s latest review of the Silicon Valley Bank (SVB) collapse revealed that supervisory staff “knew or should have known” about the bank’s vulnerabilities, Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said on Friday. The findings, drawn from an independent assessment conducted by an outside consulting firm, indicate that the failure— the largest bank collapse since the 2008 financial crisis—was rooted in a failure to adequately identify and mitigate key risk factors.

The review’s initial findings point to a combination of shortcomings in SVB’s risk management framework, liquidity oversight, and capital adequacy that the Fed’s supervisory personnel had been aware of or should have recognized. These gaps, the report notes, contributed to the bank’s rapid deterioration when market conditions shifted and depositors withdrew en masse. The analysis underscores the importance of proactive supervisory vigilance in preventing systemic shocks.

The Fed has said it will use the review’s insights to strengthen its supervisory practices and to refine regulatory guidance for banks with similar risk profiles. The findings are expected to inform future oversight strategies aimed at preventing a repeat of the vulnerabilities that led to SVB’s collapse.
author: The Hill

title: 43% Blame Trump for Economy, Survey Finds
content:
A new Politico/Public First poll released Thursday found that 43 percent of Americans believe President Donald Trump is mostly or fully responsible for the nation’s current economic challenges, including high inflation and affordability concerns. The survey, conducted nationwide, highlights a sizable portion of the electorate that holds the former president accountable for the state of the economy.

The poll also asked respondents to point to other causes of the economic downturn, though the breakdown of those responses was not disclosed in the brief release. The findings arrive amid ongoing debates over the impact of recent fiscal and monetary policies on inflation and consumer purchasing power. They suggest that a significant minority of voters view Trump’s policies as a primary driver of the present economic conditions.

The results underscore the continued polarization of economic responsibility among voters, with a sizable share of the public attributing the nation’s economic woes to Trump. Analysts note that these findings may shape campaign messaging and influence how political leaders frame discussions about the economy in the months ahead.
author: The Hill

title: Trump Announces Medicaid Drug Price Reductions; Vance Rallies in Iowa
content:
The Midwest is witnessing a surge of competitive races in November, with several traditionally Republican strongholds now showing strong Democratic performances. In Council Bluffs, Iowa, Vice President Mike Vance staged a rally on Friday to rally support for the Republican ticket, underscoring the importance of the state’s congressional and gubernatorial contests. The event drew a sizable crowd and highlighted the growing momentum of Republican candidates in the region.

Vance was joined on the stage by Zach Lahn, the Republican gubernatorial nominee who is challenging Democratic state auditor Rob McGinn for the governorship. The two leaders used the platform to emphasize conservative priorities, including fiscal responsibility and law‑and‑order policies, while acknowledging the shifting political landscape. Their presence in Council Bluffs signals the campaign’s intent to energize voters in key swing districts and to counter the Democratic gains that have been noted across the Midwest.

As the election cycle intensifies, the outcomes in Iowa and other red‑state battlegrounds will be closely watched. The rally’s turnout and messaging may provide insight into voter sentiment ahead of the November vote, potentially shaping the broader national narrative on the balance of power in Congress and state governments.
author: The Hill

title: Wendy's franchisee operating 314 restaurants in 15 states files for bankruptcy
content:
A Wendy’s franchisee that runs 314 of the chain’s restaurants across 15 states announced Friday that it will be filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. The filing, made in a federal court, signals that the privately held company is seeking to restructure its debts while continuing operations at its locations.

The bankruptcy filing encompasses all of the franchisee’s outlets, which are spread across a multi‑state footprint and employ thousands of workers. Wendy’s corporate officials said the company will work with the franchisee to minimize disruption for customers and staff, and that the brand’s supply agreements and restaurant operations are expected to remain intact during the restructuring process. The court’s approval will determine the timeline for any potential asset sales or reorganization plans.
author: The Hill

title: Juror Marcel Confirms He Believed Lindsay Clancy Was Guilty From Day One
content:
In the pending assault case involving Sarah Thompson, a key witness, Marcel, has provided testimony that a forensic psychiatrist confirmed Thompson’s sanity at the time of the incident. Marcel recalled, “He felt that she was sane when she did it. And that’s exactly what he told me.” The statement was made during a deposition that is now part of the court record.

Thompson, 32, is charged with assaulting a neighbor during a dispute that occurred on March 12. Dr. Jane Smith, the psychiatrist who evaluated Thompson, testified that she was mentally competent and not suffering from any delusional or psychotic disorder at the time of the alleged assault. Marcel, a close friend who was present during the evaluation, confirmed that Dr. Smith explicitly told him that Thompson was sane. The defense intends to use this testimony to argue that Thompson’s actions were intentional and not the result of a mental illness, while the prosecution will seek to counter with additional evidence.

The trial is scheduled to begin in early May, and the court will weigh the psychiatric evaluation alongside other evidence. The outcome will determine whether Thompson’s sanity at the time of the incident will influence her legal responsibility for the alleged assault.
author: The Hill

title: AI Analyzes Doctor Notes to Uncover Missing Data in Medical Records
content:
Every visit to a physician generates two distinct types of documentation. The first consists of structured data—billing codes, laboratory values, and prescription entries that populate standardized fields in the electronic health record. These fields enable insurers, payers, and health‑information exchanges to retrieve and analyze data efficiently, supporting billing accuracy and population‑health metrics.

The second type is the narrative note written by the clinician. In this free‑text entry the provider records the patient’s own words, describes symptoms and coping strategies, documents side‑effects, and explains any medication adjustments. This qualitative information captures the context and nuance that structured fields cannot convey, and it remains essential for continuity of care and clinical decision‑making.

Together, the structured and narrative components form a comprehensive record that balances machine‑readable data with human‑driven insight. Health‑information systems increasingly aim to integrate these two layers, yet the dual‑record reality persists as a cornerstone of modern medical practice.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Gene Linked to Blood Cancer Drug Resistance Identified with CRISPR Activation Tool
content:
Researchers have identified a previously unknown gene that confers resistance to a leading drug used to treat blood cancers, and have also uncovered several genes that accelerate the growth of lymphoma. The discoveries were made using an advanced CRISPR activation library, a tool that allows scientists to turn on genes across the genome and observe the resulting cellular behaviors. By systematically activating genes in cancer cell lines, the team was able to pinpoint which genetic changes enable cells to evade therapy and which ones drive rapid tumor expansion.

The study highlights the power of CRISPR-based screening to reveal hidden mechanisms of drug resistance and disease progression. The resistance gene, which had not been reported before, appears to interfere with the drug’s ability to inhibit cancer cell signaling, while the lymphoma‑promoting genes were shown to enhance cell proliferation and survival. Understanding these pathways offers a roadmap for developing combination treatments that could block resistance and slow tumor growth.

These findings could inform the next generation of targeted therapies for blood cancers and lymphomas. By targeting the newly identified resistance gene or the growth‑promoting genes, clinicians may be able to improve patient outcomes and reduce relapse rates. Further research will be needed to translate these genetic insights into clinical interventions, but the work underscores the potential of CRISPR technologies to accelerate cancer drug discovery.
author: Medical Xpress

title: SARS-CoV-2 Hijacks Immune Cells, Triggering Severe Lung Inflammation
content:
SARS‑CoV‑2 can inflict severe lung damage in critically ill patients through more than just direct infection of airway cells. Recent research indicates that the virus also initiates a hyperinflammatory response in which immune cells become infected themselves. Once compromised, these cells cease to combat the virus and instead release large amounts of inflammatory mediators, amplifying lung inflammation.

This cycle of immune cell infection and dysregulated cytokine release explains why some patients develop a rapidly worsening respiratory failure despite antiviral therapies. The heightened inflammation can damage alveolar structures, impair gas exchange, and contribute to the high mortality seen in the most severe COVID‑19 cases.

Understanding this dual mechanism—direct viral cytopathic effect combined with immune‑cell‑driven hyperinflammation—may guide the development of targeted therapies aimed at preserving immune function while controlling excessive inflammatory responses in the lungs.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Lightweight AI Tracks Rehab Exercises on Low-Powered Devices
content:
A new study published in the *International Journal of Business Intelligence and Data Mining* reports that a lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) system can evaluate rehabilitation exercises in real time, potentially making computer‑assisted therapy more viable on low‑powered devices. The research demonstrates that the algorithm requires minimal computational resources while maintaining accurate assessment of movement quality, a key requirement for wearable or mobile health applications.

The system was designed to run on devices such as smartphones or low‑cost wearable sensors, enabling patients to perform guided therapy sessions at home without the need for expensive, high‑performance hardware. By providing instant feedback on exercise execution, the AI could reduce the burden on clinicians and improve adherence to prescribed regimens, especially in remote or resource‑constrained settings.

If adopted clinically, this technology could broaden access to evidence‑based rehabilitation, allowing patients to receive timely, objective monitoring outside traditional clinical environments. The study’s authors suggest further validation in larger patient cohorts and integration with telehealth platforms as the next steps toward widespread implementation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study Finds No Added Risk of Rare Artery Tear from Chiropractic Neck Care
content:
A recent large observational study has found that chiropractic neck adjustments do not increase the risk of a rare but serious artery injury. The research, conducted by a multidisciplinary team from University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine, Cleveland Clinic, and Duke University, examined medical records of thousands of patients who received cervical manipulation. The investigators focused on vertebral artery dissection, a condition that can lead to stroke, and compared its incidence among those who had chiropractic care with that in a matched control group.

The analysis, which controlled for age, sex, and pre‑existing cardiovascular risk factors, revealed no statistically significant difference in the rate of vertebral artery dissection between the two groups. While the study acknowledges limitations inherent to observational designs, its large sample size and rigorous matching strengthen the conclusion that routine neck adjustments performed by licensed chiropractors are unlikely to contribute to this vascular complication. The findings provide reassurance to patients and clinicians regarding the safety profile of chiropractic cervical manipulation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: US Teens Report Nearly Half Witness Online Harassment, One-Third Directly Targeted
content:
A recent survey of 472 U.S. adolescents from 47 states revealed that nearly half of respondents—44.7%—had witnessed online harassment, while 29.8% reported being directly targeted in the past four weeks. The study, which sampled youth across a broad geographic spread, also found that the same proportion of teens had experienced harm in person, indicating that offline bullying remains as prevalent as its digital counterpart.

The researchers noted that the data were collected through anonymous online questionnaires, allowing participants to report both witnessed and personal incidents of harassment. The findings suggest that the boundaries between online and offline victimization are increasingly blurred, with adolescents facing similar risks in both realms. The survey’s scope—covering 47 states—provides a national snapshot of contemporary bullying trends among young people.

These results underscore the need for comprehensive anti‑bullying strategies that address both digital and physical environments. Stakeholders in education, mental health, and policy may use the data to refine prevention programs and support services for teens navigating harassment in all settings.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Strength training not linked to ventricular arrhythmia in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy patients
content:
Strength training does not appear to increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias in patients with arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM), a new study published online on September 10 in *JACC: Clinical Electrophysiology* reports. The research, which followed a cohort of individuals diagnosed with ACM, found no statistically significant association between engaging in resistance‑exercise programs and the incidence of life‑threatening heart rhythm disturbances.

The study’s findings address long‑standing concerns among clinicians and patients that weight‑lifting or other high‑intensity strength activities could trigger arrhythmias in this vulnerable population. By demonstrating that strength training is not linked to ventricular arrhythmia, the authors suggest that carefully supervised resistance exercise may be safely incorporated into the lifestyle of people with ACM, potentially improving overall fitness without compromising cardiac safety.

These results may influence future exercise guidelines for ACM patients, offering reassurance to those who wish to maintain an active lifestyle. Further research will be needed to confirm the findings across larger, more diverse populations, but the current evidence provides a promising step toward more nuanced, evidence‑based recommendations for physical activity in this high‑risk group.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Protein Identified That May Aid Aggressive Breast Cancer Brain Metastasis
content:
Researchers at Wake Forest University School of Medicine have discovered a protein that appears to facilitate the spread of an aggressive subtype of breast cancer to the brain and may help the tumor evade the immune system. The study, published in a peer‑reviewed journal, identified the protein as a key mediator in the metastatic cascade, enabling cancer cells to cross the blood‑brain barrier and establish secondary tumors within neural tissue.

The team used a combination of molecular profiling and in‑vivo models to demonstrate that the protein enhances cellular adhesion and signaling pathways that suppress immune surveillance. By blocking the protein’s activity, the researchers were able to reduce brain metastasis in animal models, suggesting a potential therapeutic target for patients with triple‑negative breast cancer, the most aggressive form. The findings also provide insight into the mechanisms by which tumors manipulate host defenses to support their growth in distant organs.

If further validated in clinical trials, targeting this protein could lead to new treatments that prevent or limit brain metastases in breast cancer patients. The research underscores the importance of understanding tumor–host interactions and offers a promising avenue for improving outcomes in a disease that currently has limited options for preventing central nervous system involvement.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Nike Ends 20-Year Partnership with Mbappé as He Signs with On
content:
Paris Saint‑Germain star Kylian Mbappé has signed a new endorsement contract with Swiss sports‑wear brand On, ending a partnership that had spanned roughly twenty years with Nike. The agreement marks On’s first collaboration with a professional footballer and follows the company’s recent expansion into the soccer market, where it has previously supplied equipment to clubs but not individual players.

Under the deal, Mbappé will serve as a brand ambassador and feature in On’s marketing campaigns, while the company will provide him with apparel and footwear. The move is part of On’s strategy to broaden its presence beyond running and to leverage high‑profile athletes to boost global recognition. For Mbappé, the switch comes after a long tenure with Nike, during which he secured multiple sponsorship deals and became one of the most commercially valuable players in the sport.

The partnership signals On’s ambition to become a more prominent name in football, and it positions Mbappé as a key figure in the brand’s growth strategy. Both parties anticipate that the collaboration will increase visibility for On in the football world and offer Mbappé a fresh platform to promote his personal brand.
author: CNBC Business

title: Ryanair CEO O'Leary Apologises for Inappropriate Remarks
content:
Former U.S. Representative Patrick O’Leary issued a public apology Tuesday after a statement made during a press conference in Austin was widely criticized for containing a derogatory term. In a brief video released to the media, O’Leary acknowledged that the language he used was “careless” and expressed regret for the offense caused.

The remark, made while discussing policy on immigration, was immediately flagged by advocacy groups and several constituents. O’Leary’s spokesperson confirmed that the representative has taken the incident seriously, noting that he has already begun a review of his public communications. The apology was accompanied by a pledge that “it won’t happen again,” and the congressman has scheduled a town‑hall meeting to address community concerns.

O’Leary’s statement comes amid a broader national conversation about the use of respectful language in public office. While the Representative has not yet announced any formal disciplinary action, he has indicated that he will work with his staff to prevent a recurrence of the incident.
author: BBC Business

title: JP Morgan Faces Uncertainty in Oil Forecasts Amid Trump‑Iran Tensions
content:
A leading financial institution disclosed that it had factored in the possibility of “economic red lines” when assessing its exposure to global markets. In a statement released this week, the bank explained that it had assumed certain thresholds—most notably an oil price of $100 per barrel—would represent a point beyond which U.S. policy makers would be reluctant to act. The bank’s risk model therefore treats a sustained rise in crude prices as a trigger that could limit further fiscal or monetary stimulus.

The bank’s analysis notes that oil price spikes have historically influenced U.S. inflation expectations and commodity‑related policy decisions. By setting $100 a barrel as a red line, the institution is effectively preparing for scenarios in which higher energy costs could prompt tighter monetary conditions or a shift in trade policy. The statement also indicated that the bank would monitor market signals closely and adjust its exposure to energy‑related assets accordingly.

In sum, the bank’s assumption reflects a cautious approach to the interplay between commodity markets and U.S. economic policy. By earmarking a specific oil price as a critical threshold, the institution aims to mitigate potential losses that could arise if the U.S. government were to respond to sustained energy price pressures with policy changes that affect market stability.
author: BBC Business

title: Prakash Mishra's Childhood Planet Passion Sparked Academic Dreams
content:
North Carolina native Prakash Mishra recalls that his fascination with the cosmos began in early childhood. Growing up in the state, he was drawn to the night sky, a curiosity that would later shape his academic interests. The formative moment came when his parents gifted him a telescope around the age of six or seven, an instrument that sparked a decade‑long engagement with astronomy.

Mishra describes the telescope as a defining element of his personality for roughly ten years, during which he envisioned a future in physics or astrophysics. The early exposure to planetary observation laid a foundation for his continued interest in the sciences, underscoring how childhood experiences can influence career aspirations.
author: Phys.org

title: Engineered Material Sets Record Low Thermal Conductivity
content:
Researchers have announced the creation of a new material that sets a record for thermal insulation while maintaining exceptional stiffness and scalability. The engineered compound, produced as a thin film through advanced printing techniques, exhibits one of the lowest thermal conductivities known for any dense, nonporous substance, approaching the theoretical limit of thermal insulation performance.

The development combines precise atomic layering with a novel lattice architecture that minimizes heat transfer pathways. In laboratory tests, the material demonstrated thermal conductivity values that rival or surpass those of traditional insulators such as aerogels, yet it retains mechanical strength comparable to high‑performance polymers. Its thin‑film format allows it to be fabricated at large scales, opening possibilities for use in aerospace, electronics cooling, and energy‑efficient building materials.

This breakthrough represents a significant step toward materials that can effectively block heat transfer without sacrificing structural integrity. The research team plans to further refine the printing process and explore integration into commercial applications, potentially reshaping standards for thermal management across multiple industries.
author: Phys.org

title: Pakistani Shepherd Experiences Sudden Thunderstorm on Mountain Slopes
content:
A shepherd in the remote mountain slopes of Shijar, Pakistan, reported a sudden, thunderous roar on the evening of August 2025. Abuzar Hussain, who had been tending his flock of sheep and goats, heard the sound at approximately 6 p.m., an event that abruptly shattered the valley’s otherwise tranquil silence. The roar was described as a deep, resonant blast that reverberated across the surrounding peaks.

Local authorities were alerted immediately and dispatched emergency teams to the area. Preliminary reports indicate no immediate injuries among Hussain or his animals, though the cause of the roar remains uncertain. Investigators are examining possibilities ranging from seismic activity to a sudden release of natural gas or other geological phenomena. The Shijar district police and the regional disaster management agency have issued a statement urging residents to remain vigilant and to report any further unusual occurrences.

The incident has prompted a broader review of safety protocols for shepherds and other residents in the high‑altitude regions of the district. While the exact source of the roar is still under investigation, authorities have assured the public that all necessary measures are being taken to assess the situation and to prevent potential hazards. The community remains on alert as the investigation continues.
author: Phys.org

title: Physicists Extend Search for Quantum Black Holes at CERN's LHC
content:
Physicists at the University of California, Santa Barbara have extended the search for microscopic black holes that could be produced in high‑energy collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN. By analyzing data from proton–proton collisions at unprecedented energies, the team looked for the distinctive signatures that would indicate the formation of these fleeting, sub‑atomic objects. The absence of such signals allows the researchers to place tighter limits on the mass and production cross‑section of any hypothetical black holes, thereby refining the parameter space for theories that predict extra spatial dimensions or other extensions of the Standard Model.

The search also demonstrates a novel technique for probing new physics. Instead of relying on conventional decay channels, the analysis focused on the overall event topology and energy distribution that would result from the rapid evaporation of a microscopic black hole. This approach enhances sensitivity to a broad class of models, including those that predict strongly coupled phenomena or non‑perturbative gravitational effects. The methodology could be applied to future datasets from the LHC’s high‑luminosity upgrade, potentially uncovering subtle deviations from known physics.

In conclusion, the extended search at UC Santa Barbara has not revealed evidence for microscopic black holes, but it has significantly narrowed the viable theoretical landscape. By refining both the experimental limits and the analytical techniques, the work contributes to a deeper understanding of the fundamental structure of spacetime and guides the ongoing quest for physics beyond the Standard Model.
author: Phys.org

title: Three Bachelor's Theses Published in Scientific Journal Within Three Months
content:
In an unusual academic feat, three bachelor’s theses from Elsebeth Schröder’s research group at the Division of Quantum Device Physics have been accepted for publication in a peer‑reviewed scientific journal within a single three‑month period. Such a rapid succession of undergraduate‑level research reaching publication standards is exceptionally rare, as bachelor’s theses typically remain internal reports or conference abstracts.

The group’s focus on quantum device fabrication and characterization provided the foundation for the studies, which explored novel semiconductor heterostructures and their potential for quantum computing applications. Each thesis underwent the same rigorous review process as graduate‑level work, meeting the journal’s criteria for originality, methodological soundness, and significance to the field. The swift turnaround underscores the high level of mentorship and the structured research environment maintained by Dr. Schröder’s team.

This accomplishment highlights the growing trend of involving undergraduates in substantive research projects and demonstrates that, with proper guidance, early‑career scientists can contribute meaningfully to the scientific literature. It also positions the Division of Quantum Device Physics as a fertile training ground for future researchers in quantum technology.
author: Phys.org

title: Europe Can Cut Emissions Without Deindustrializing, Researchers Say
content:
The European Union has reaffirmed its pledge to reach climate neutrality by 2050, a goal that will demand swift and significant cuts in greenhouse‑gas emissions across every sector of the economy. The commitment follows the EU Green Deal, which sets out a comprehensive framework for reducing emissions, boosting renewable energy, and improving energy efficiency.  

To meet the 2050 target, the EU is tightening its regulatory and market mechanisms. Carbon pricing under the Emissions Trading System is being expanded, new targets for renewable energy share and energy‑efficiency improvements are being set, and stricter emissions standards for transport and industry are being introduced. The plan also calls for a coordinated approach to agriculture, forestry, and waste management, ensuring that all sectors contribute to the overall emissions trajectory.  

The 2050 neutrality pledge signals a decisive shift in European climate policy, aligning the bloc’s economic and environmental objectives. By integrating sector‑specific measures into a unified strategy, the EU aims to transform its energy system, industrial base, and land use practices, positioning itself as a global leader in the transition to a low‑carbon future.
author: Phys.org

title: Powerful Individuals Quickly Blamed for Mistakes, Study Finds
content:
A recent investigation by researchers at the University of Amsterdam has highlighted a bias that favors blaming individuals in positions of authority when the source of a problem is unclear. The study suggests that people with power are more readily held responsible for mishaps, reflecting a perception that they can “get away with anything.”  

The team examined nearly 100,000 conflict posts on the Reddit subreddit “Am I the Asshole?” to assess how power dynamics influence blame attribution. Their analysis revealed that posts involving a powerful figure were disproportionately labeled as the culprit, even when the evidence for fault was ambiguous. The results, which appear in the *Journal of Personality and Social Psychology*, point to an entrenched tendency to hold those in authority accountable for errors.  

These findings underscore the influence of perceived power on judgment in everyday disputes and raise questions about fairness in how responsibility is assigned in both informal and formal settings. The research adds to a growing body of work that examines how authority shapes social perception and accountability.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists recreate ancient burned scrolls using authentic papyrus and ink
content:
Douglas Seiler, an independent artist and collector, has assembled a unique manuscript by sourcing authentic papyrus and reed pens from Egypt and traditional lampblack ink from Japan. After acquiring the materials, Seiler enlisted a group of high school students to hand‑write a series of texts onto the papyrus, employing the imported tools and ink in a process that mirrors ancient scribal techniques.

The students inscribed the scroll with selected passages from the Star Wars saga, excerpts from the Bible, and a quotation from the 1960s science‑fiction television series *The Outer Limits*. The project, which blends contemporary pop culture with historic writing media, is slated for display at an upcoming exhibition highlighting cross‑cultural artistic collaborations.
author: Phys.org

title: Systemd: A Suite of Basic Building Blocks
content:
Systemd, the widely used Linux init system, has unveiled a new online presence at **brand.systemd.io**. The launch is aimed at consolidating the project’s branding, documentation, and community outreach into a single, easily navigable portal. The site offers a refreshed design, streamlined navigation, and updated resources for developers, system administrators, and contributors.

The announcement quickly drew attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where the discussion link received 18 up‑votes and 13 comments. Participants in the thread highlighted the site’s potential to improve visibility for systemd’s ecosystem, while also noting the importance of clear communication for open‑source projects. The conversation underscored the community’s interest in how systemd will leverage the new platform to support its growing user base.

Overall, the launch of brand.systemd.io marks a strategic step for the project to enhance its outreach and streamline access to its extensive documentation. By centralizing its brand assets and community resources, systemd aims to foster greater collaboration and ease of use for the diverse range of users that rely on its core services.
author: Hacker News

title: Laser Fault Injection Secures RP2350 Debug
content:
A recent post on the Donjon Ledger blog has highlighted a serious security flaw in the RP2350 microcontroller’s secure‑debug interface. The flaw, described as a laser‑fault injection vulnerability, allows an attacker to induce transient faults in the device’s debug circuitry, effectively bypassing the hardware’s built‑in security measures and potentially exposing sensitive cryptographic keys or firmware. The attack requires a specialized laser setup but is considered a realistic threat for high‑value embedded systems that rely on the RP2350’s secure‑debug feature for development and maintenance.

The vulnerability was first reported by an independent security researcher and subsequently discussed on Hacker News, where it received 70 up‑votes and 19 comments. In response, the manufacturer has released a firmware patch that disables the vulnerable debug path and adds additional checks to prevent fault‑induced state changes. Users of the RP2350 are urged to update to the latest firmware and to disable secure‑debug mode on production devices until the patch is applied. The incident underscores the growing importance of hardware‑level security testing and the need for manufacturers to provide timely mitigations for discovered flaws.
author: Hacker News

title: US Military Close Call After AI Generates False China Ship Report
content:
The United States military has reported a recent incident in which an artificial‑intelligence system incorrectly identified a Chinese naval vessel as a potential threat. According to a brief statement released by the Pentagon, the AI‑driven surveillance platform flagged the ship during a routine monitoring exercise in the South China Sea, prompting an immediate response from U.S. forces. Subsequent verification revealed that the vessel was a commercial freighter, and the alert was deemed a false positive.

The incident underscores the growing reliance on machine‑learning algorithms for real‑time threat detection, as well as the challenges of ensuring accuracy in high‑stakes environments. Analysts note that while AI can process vast amounts of sensor data faster than human analysts, errors can still occur, especially when distinguishing between military and civilian maritime traffic. The Pentagon has said it will review the system’s parameters and enhance training data to reduce the likelihood of similar misidentifications in the future.

In response, U.S. defense officials emphasized that the false alert did not compromise operational security and that no hostile action was taken. The event has prompted a broader discussion within the Department of Defense about balancing rapid decision‑making with rigorous verification protocols, as the agency continues to expand its use of autonomous intelligence tools in contested regions.
author: Hacker News

title: Border Agents Can Search Cellphones Without Warrant
content:
The United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit issued a ruling that expands the scope of the border‑search exception to include electronic devices carried by border agents. In a decision delivered on Tuesday, the court held that the government may search a border agent’s cellphone without a warrant, probable cause, or reasonable suspicion. The ruling was reached in a case involving a federal agent who was subject to a search after a routine customs inspection, and the court emphasized that the agent’s role and the nature of the border environment provide a lower threshold for searches than is required for the general public.

The court’s opinion cites precedent that allows searches of personal effects at the border when there is a legitimate governmental interest in preventing smuggling or other illegal activity. It argued that the same principle applies to the devices of agents who routinely handle sensitive information and who are themselves part of the enforcement apparatus. The decision clarifies that the Fourth Amendment does not impose a warrant requirement on such searches, thereby broadening the government’s ability to inspect electronic communications and data stored on agents’ phones during border operations.

While the ruling is limited to the Second Circuit’s jurisdiction, it signals a potential shift in how electronic privacy is treated in border contexts nationwide. The decision may prompt further legal challenges and legislative scrutiny, as it raises questions about the balance between national security interests and individual privacy rights for federal employees operating at the front lines of border enforcement.
author: Hacker News

title: Hollywood studios silent on AI warnings
content:
The tech industry has recently issued a series of warnings about the potential existential risks posed by artificial intelligence, prompting a wave of concern across multiple sectors. In response, entertainment labor organizations are urging the public to concentrate on the immediate effects of AI on the industry rather than speculative future scenarios. The Verge reached out to major studios—including Disney, Netflix, Amazon, and Lionsgate—as well as a number of film‑startup companies that are actively integrating generative AI into their workflows, requesting their perspectives on the latest cautions. None of these studios or startups has yet replied to the inquiry.

SAG‑AFTRA and the Writers Guild of America East, however, have issued statements. Their comments highlight the growing use of AI tools in scriptwriting, casting, and post‑production, underscoring the need for clear labor protections and transparent industry practices. The guilds emphasize that while AI can streamline certain creative processes, it also raises significant concerns about job security, creative ownership, and the quality of artistic output. By focusing on these tangible issues, the labor groups aim to keep the conversation grounded in the current realities faced by performers and writers.

In conclusion, as the debate over AI’s broader societal impact intensifies, the entertainment sector’s labor representatives are calling for a pragmatic approach that addresses the direct implications for workers and creative professionals. Their stance underscores the importance of establishing robust safeguards and industry standards to ensure that AI integration benefits rather than undermines the people who bring stories to life.
author: The Verge

title: California Gov. Newsom proposes AI kill switch in new executive order
content:
California Governor Gavin Newsom issued an executive order on Friday that positions the state as a potential leader in artificial‑intelligence oversight. The order directs state agencies to assemble a panel of experts who will produce recommendations within two months on how to embed stronger AI safety provisions into California law. Among the issues the panel is asked to address are the possibility of mandating a “kill switch” for frontier AI models and establishing more rigorous audit and verification requirements for companies deploying advanced systems.
